Resolves #17885

🌿 *The synthetic pipeline keeps the Neo world; the border crossing gets a customs form — and what a consumer once hand-rolled on the main thread became a declaration nothing executes.*

`Neo.main.addon.NativeDragSource` (new): real HTML5 drags whose `DataTransfer` fills from worker-declared JSON — a `delegate` selector, a mime→attribute-template map, an optional `effectAllowed`. `Neo.component.Base` gains the `nativeDragZone_` config that forwards the declaration on mount and retires it on destroy. The partition with the synthetic pipeline is now a one-authority contract: `sensor/Mouse` consults the addon's `claimsEvent()` and declines gestures on registered sources — so the sensor's `dragstart` suppression never kills a native payload, and `neo-drag-active` (the iframe shield's hook) is never stamped for a drag whose purpose is to land on an iframe. The drag system's README gains the two-worlds contract section.

Evidence: L3 achieved at exact head — a REAL browser drag (`page.dragAndDrop`) carries the declared payload into a live drop target, with types, template payloads, and `effectAllowed: copy` all asserted from the LIVE drag data store in `dragover`/`drop`; plus the full-worker-stack listener-seam witness, 17 unit specs (addon mechanics, producer lifecycle incl. window migration, the `useDomIds:false` red control), and the sensor-partition mutant-killer pair. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | browser witness `component/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs`: real component + `nativeDragZone` config → real addon over the remote pipeline → document-listener mousedown arms, dispatched dragstart fills both declared types from the live DOM node; plus the addon unit mechanics and the new producer-lifecycle spec (`unit/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs`: mount gating, pre-mount reset, replacement, destroy, window migration with the old-realm unregister asserted) |
| AC-2 | REAL-drag witness: `effectAllowed: copy` read from the LIVE store in `dragover` during `page.dragAndDrop`; unit: explicit `move` honored, default `copy` asserted at the fill seam |
| AC-3 | unit, mutant-killing pair: `the sensor declines a gesture the addon claims — and claims the same gesture once unregistered` — drives the REAL `Mouse.prototype.onMouseDown` with a `neo-draggable` ancestor in the path; decline proves neither claim nor `dragstart` suppression install (both live only inside the claimed branch) |
| AC-4 | unit: arm-on-press / disarm-on-gesture-end asserted; DOM between gestures carries no `draggable` |
| AC-5 | structural + AC-3's test: `neo-drag-active` is added only inside the sensor's claimed branch (`Mouse.mjs`), and the partition test proves registered-source gestures never enter that branch |
| AC-6 | full unit suite green at the branch head (receipt in Test Evidence) |
| AC-7 | `src/main/draggable/README.md` — the two-worlds contract section, naming the one-authority partition and both load-bearing consequences |

## Deltas from ticket
One substantive: the ticket's sketch had the addon deferring to the sensors AND the sensors sparing registered nodes — mutual deferral, which on an overlap (a registered leaf under a `neo-draggable` ancestor) leaves a dead node both sides decline. Implemented instead with ONE authority: the registration wins, the sensor consults `claimsEvent()`, the addon defers to nobody. The overlap becomes a defined state; the README section documents the tiebreak.

## Test Evidence
Addon spec 11/11 (incl. the pre-draggable claim/arm-agreement pair and the useDomIds:false red control), producer-lifecycle spec 6/6, browser witness 1/1 (components project, real page). Full unit suite: **2140 passed + 27 skipped = 2167, zero failures, parallel mode** at `616c34c22a` (the round-2 head, publicly reachable); browser witnesses 2/2 in the components project — `component.Base` and the Mouse sensor are maximal-importer surfaces, so the full run is the coverage claim, not a targeted subset. The sensor-partition test is deliberately a positive/negative pair on the same gesture — the consult line is the only discriminator, so its mutation reds the pair.

## Post-Merge Validation
None — every close-target AC verifies pre-merge. Consumer-workspace adoption (replacing the hand-rolled reference addon with the config) follows in the private lane that motivated the ticket, receipts to #17885 after merge.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-08-30T21:43:59Z

## Author response — 3/3 Required Actions discharged, no contract changes beyond the repairs you named

**RA-1 (claim/arm divergence on pre-draggable nodes):** ✅ exactly the hole you described — my `!node.draggable` arm-guard let `claimsEvent` make the sensor yield while `armed` stayed null, and the pre-draggable node then dragged with an unfilled store and no cleanup owner. Repaired: a registered match arms **unconditionally**; `armed.addedAttribute` records whether the addon added the attribute; the fill matches by node regardless of who owned `draggable`; terminal restores **only addon-owned DOM state** (an author's attribute survives the gesture). New unit: *"a node that was ALREADY draggable still arms, still fills, and keeps its attribute on terminal"* — asserting `armed !== null` right after the press is the mutant-killer for the divergence (re-adding the old guard reds it while `claimsEvent` stays true).

**RA-2 (producer lifecycle + DOM identity):** ✅ all five surfaces:
- Owner resolution now rides `Neo.main.DomAccess.getElement()` — the dual-identity authority (`id` and `useDomIds:false`'s `data-neo-id`), with the in-code comment naming why `getElementById` silently loses half the supported apps. Runtime lookup keeps the seam swappable for the unit harness.
- `registerNativeDragZone()` / `retireNativeDragZone()` replace the inline afterSet: sends are **generation-guarded** (a pending mount-gated send whose generation was superseded drops instead of resurrecting stale state), and the component records `nativeDragZoneWindowId` — **the realm that holds the registration** — so retire addresses the old window after a transfer, not the current one.
- `afterSetWindowId` migrates: retire in the old realm, re-register gated on the **new** mount.
- `destroy` retires via the same path; a never-registered declaration (pre-mount reset) makes zero remote calls.
- Behavioral coverage: new `unit/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs` — mount-gating, pre-mount reset, reactive replacement (retire→register sequence asserted), destroy, **window transfer with the unregister's `windowId` asserted as the OLD realm**, and the never-registered destroy.

**RA-3 (browser witness + evidence truth-sync):** ✅ new `component/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs` — a real component created over `Neo.worker.App.createNeoInstance` with the `nativeDragZone` config, the declaration reaching the **real addon over the remote pipeline** (the empty-viewport fixture now loads `NativeDragSource` alongside the defaults), and the whole interaction entering through **real document listeners**: `mousedown` arms (attribute observed), a dispatched `dragstart` fills both declared types via template substitution from the live DOM node, `neo-drag-active` is absent, `dragend` restores the attribute. **One documented platform boundary:** Chromium accepts the `effectAllowed` write only inside a real user-initiated drag's read/write data store — on a constructed `DataTransfer` it reads back `none` even mid-dispatch, so that single field stays proven at the unit layer (the spec carries the boundary note in place). PR body's Evidence declaration truth-synced to the exact-head receipts.

**Rode along:** the MaxListeners warning the new lifecycle spec surfaced was real hygiene — the addon now keeps its bound listeners and removes them in `destroy()`.

Evidence at the new head: addon spec 10/10, lifecycle spec 6/6, browser witness 1/1, full unit suite receipt in the PR body. Ready for re-review.
